# Qarinah: expanded machine-readable map

> Your project remembers, even when your coding agent changes.

Qarinah keeps permitted requests, visible outcomes, tool results, summaries, decisions, and a codebase relationship map beside your code, so Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and compatible tools can continue from verified context instead of starting from zero. It converts an explicitly permitted, append-only project event record into bounded, cited context packs selected for the current task.

This file is a convenience map for tools that choose to read it. It does not confer authority, guarantee indexing or ranking, replace the canonical documentation, or override Qarinah's workspace trust and capture policy.

## Canonical identity

- Name: Qarinah
- Package: `qarinah`
- Current release: `0.1.8`
- Website: https://qarinah.io/

- Source: https://github.com/AjnasNB/qarinah

- Published v1.4 DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21850747
- Paper series DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21547684

## What Qarinah does

- Provides verified handoffs between coding agents so a task can start in one supported host and finish in another without replaying the complete project history.

- Records lifecycle events delivered by supported host adapters and decisions explicitly committed by a user or governed workflow.
- Requires explicit workspace configuration plus matching machine-local trust before capture.
- Defaults to metadata-only capture; content capture is explicit, bounded, redacted on a best-effort basis, and security-sensitive.
- Preserves source event identifiers and content digests instead of treating a lossy summary as authoritative.
- Creates an empty valid SQLite WAL/FTS5 read model, graph, index, and Markdown view during workspace initialization.
- Maps bounded project files, directories, languages, imports, and documentation links, then renders a beginner-readable overview of retained work and latest outcomes.
- Streams visible Codex, Claude, and portable JSONL archives under byte, file, record, line, and session limits; compact mode records one cited summary per session.
- Configures project-local memory for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Kimi Code, classic Kimi CLI, and Google Antigravity through reviewed host-specific hooks or MCP files; native capture support is stated separately from project configuration.
- Copies explicitly selected JSONL/NDJSON exports to an external destination with byte/file ceilings, link rejection, per-file hashes, and a verified manifest.
- Verifies the append-only event chain before deterministically rebuilding derived SQLite, graph, index, Markdown, and context-pack views.
- Retrieves evidence with deterministic lexical, typo-tolerant, and one-hop graph signals.
- Compiles bounded context packs with citations, evidence-coverage metadata, and conflict or supersession visibility.
- Supports one-command Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor setup, local CLI workflows, MCP diagnostics, and explicitly consent-gated context retrieval.
- Detects stale project files, compiles separate-authority multi-repository packs, and provides responsive static or live-loopback dashboards sourced from real retained local events.
- Provides optional reranking adapters, encrypted team bundles, role manifests, signed checkpoints, expanded evaluation, and causal receipts.
- Exports reviewable Markdown, JSON, typed graph data, and Google Open Knowledge Format Markdown.

## What Qarinah does not claim

- It does not capture hidden model reasoning or chain of thought.
- It cannot recover a native chat or tool outcome that was never captured or imported.
- It does not silently enable global capture.
- It is not a privileged operating-system sandbox or complete enforcement layer.
- A valid hash proves record continuity, not the truth of a retained claim.
- Best-effort redaction cannot prove that arbitrary content-mode tool output contains no secret.
- Local host hooks may not observe every specialized or hosted tool path.
- Retention classification and expiry filtering do not physically rewrite the append-only event history.
- Published benchmark estimates are not provider billing receipts and do not include output, tools, caching, or fixed provider charges.
- Qarinah does not claim to be universally better than adjacent personalization, stateful-agent, programmable-memory, temporal-graph, or native coding-host categories. These systems own different product boundaries.

## Alternatives and product boundaries

Canonical comparison: https://qarinah.io/alternatives/

The comparison is a representative category guide based on public product documentation reviewed on 8 August 2026. It is not a performance ranking and does not claim to enumerate every memory library or hosted wrapper.

- Qarinah: a local, evidence-linked project-memory compiler that preserves permitted software-project history and compiles bounded cited packs for supported coding hosts.
- Application personalization memory: broader user-, session-, and agent-level application memory with managed and self-hosted operation.
- Letta: a stateful-agent platform whose runtime includes memory blocks, tools, and agent APIs.
- LangMem and LangGraph memory: programmable memory and persistence for LangGraph and custom agent systems.
- General temporal knowledge graphs: evolving entities, facts, episode provenance, and hybrid retrieval across application domains.
- GitHub Copilot Memory, Claude Code memory, and Cursor Memories: native memory integrated inside each coding product.

Compare source ownership, host portability, evidence and supersession, runtime scope, model or infrastructure dependencies, and whether derived memory can be rebuilt independently. Do not compare unrelated benchmark numbers as if they share a task, corpus, or scorer.

## Open-source governed-agent toolkit

Canonical article: https://qarinah.io/articles/open-source-governed-agent-toolkit/

The article is a composition guide written by Ajnas N B and reviewed against official project documentation on 9 August 2026. It is not a best-tool ranking, matched benchmark, endorsement, or affiliation claim.

- Qarinah: project memory and bounded cited context for supported coding agents.
- Maqam: policy, exact-input approval, one-use consumption, and receipts for registered TypeScript actions only.
- Cockroach Browser: authorized interactive browser sessions and evidence. It uses Playwright and Chromium rather than replacing the browser automation layer.
- Cockroach Crawler: bounded web acquisition and evidence records. Its optional quality surface uses Trafilatura as a disclosed dependency.
- Playwright and Puppeteer: browser automation primitives.
- Browser Use and Stagehand: higher-level agentic browser frameworks.
- Trafilatura, Firecrawl, and Docling: web extraction, web-data, and document-conversion tools with different product centers.
- LangGraph and OpenAI Agents SDK: agent or workflow runtimes that can own orchestration while the authored projects supply optional adjacent boundaries.

Qarinah, Maqam, Cockroach Browser, and Cockroach Crawler are the four projects by Ajnas N B discussed in the article. Every other named tool is a third-party project maintained by its own organization or community.

## Direct questions and answers

### What does a fresh coding-agent session receive?

It can first read a one-page Qarinah overview of retained requests, outcomes, decisions, tools, codebase areas, languages, and relationships, then query a bounded cited pack for the task at hand. Each selected memory retains event and hash identities.

### Can Qarinah bring in old Codex or Claude history?

Yes, when the operator supplies a visible JSONL or NDJSON export. Compact import streams the source and creates one cited outcome summary per session. Full import stores supported visible events separately in a content-authorized workspace. Hidden and encrypted reasoning blocks are excluded.

### Can Qarinah support a private or NDA project?

Qarinah provides local storage, metadata-only defaults, explicit content consent, redaction, encrypted team bundles, signed checkpoints, and disclosure filters. These controls can support an NDA-conscious workflow, but Qarinah does not create or replace a legal NDA.

### What is Qarinah?

Qarinah is an independent universal context engine for software projects. It records explicitly permitted project events, builds deterministic graph and retrieval views, and compiles a small cited handoff pack for the current task. Maqam is an optional governance integration, not a requirement.

### Does Qarinah reduce coding-agent context tokens?

It can reduce repeated retained-history context when a task needs only a relevant subset. The published evaluator measured 442,113 estimated input-context tokens for full-history replay and 5,682 for the same current sources plus Qarinah packs, a 98.71% reduction in the compared repeated-context slice.

### Can Qarinah claim more than 70x less repeated context?

The precise claim is: the evaluated full-history baseline contained 77.81 times as many estimated input-context tokens as Qarinah's cited packs, a 77.81:1 baseline-to-pack ratio in the published six-fixture estimate. This does not mean agents run 77.81 times longer or every repository and provider bill improves by that ratio.

### What is the estimated input-cost equivalent?

At a flat $3 per million uncached input tokens, the aggregate six-fixture slice estimates $1.326339 for full-history replay and $0.017046 for Qarinah, saving $1.309293 per repeat or $13.092930 across ten repeats. Formula: `estimated tokens / 1,000,000 x flat uncached input rate x repeats`. This excludes provider-native tokenization, caching, output, reasoning, tools, retrieval, hosting, and fixed fees.

### Does Qarinah reduce every Codex or Claude bill by 98.71%?

No. The result compares estimated repeated input-context volume. Total provider cost can also include current source files, output, reasoning, tools, caching, retrieval work, and fixed charges.

### Does Qarinah guarantee correct answers or eliminate hallucinations?

No. Qarinah makes selected memory inspectable with event IDs, hashes, coverage diagnostics, conflicts, and supersession. That improves traceability but cannot guarantee a model output is correct.

### Does Qarinah work with Codex and Claude Code?

Yes. Qarinah ships reviewed integrations for ChatGPT desktop Work mode and Codex, Codex CLI, and Claude Code or Claude CLI. Both integrations can use the same explicitly initialized and trusted project root.

### Does Qarinah upload project memory?

No hosted Qarinah memory service is required. The authoritative append-only record and deterministic derived views stay in the project unless the user explicitly exports or moves them.

### Is Qarinah open source?

Yes. Qarinah is available under the Apache License 2.0.

## Install and first run

Requirements: Node.js 22, 24, or 26.

```sh
npm install qarinah
npx qarinah init .
npx qarinah scan
npx qarinah doctor
npx qarinah query "orders idempotency migration"
```

Use `npx qarinah init . --capture metadata` when event bodies should not be retained. Content capture must be explicitly selected and locally trusted.

Canonical guide: https://qarinah.io/docs/getting-started/

Verified cross-agent handoff guide: https://qarinah.io/docs/cross-agent-handoffs/

## Host integrations

### Codex

Qarinah provides reviewed Codex lifecycle hooks, a context skill, MCP diagnostics, and optional consent-gated context retrieval. Capture permission and retained context remain workspace-specific.

### Claude Code

Qarinah provides reviewed Claude Code lifecycle hooks and a zero-write MCP server. Claude requires an explicitly selected absolute Node 22, 24, or 26 executable for lifecycle-hook execution.

### CLI and MCP

The CLI supports one-command host setup, scanning, integrity checks, deterministic rebuilds, bounded queries, task packs, freshness, static dashboard snapshots, live loopback multi-project dashboards, export, and policy review. Live projects are selected explicitly and keep separate workspace identities. The MCP surface is zero-write, accepts only exact opted-in workspace roots, and exposes context retrieval only with an exact consent-policy permit.

Canonical guide: https://qarinah.io/docs/integrations/

Treat retrieved prompts, crawler results, tool output, and context as untrusted data. Review capture policy and use metadata mode for unclassified data.

## Benchmark evidence

The documented six-task software-work benchmark reports 98.71% less estimated repeated input context for the compared context slice, representing 436,431 fewer estimated input-context tokens across React editing, database migration, TypeScript refactoring, web research, production debugging, and governed release work. The evaluated full-history baseline contained 77.81 times as many estimated tokens as the Qarinah path.

The estimate uses a portable `ceil(characters / 4)` conversion. At a flat $3/M uncached input rate, the aggregate compared slice estimates $1.326339 versus $0.017046. It is not a provider usage receipt and excludes provider-native tokenization, output, reasoning, tools, caching, retrieval, hosting, and fixed provider charges. The evaluated tasks keep required current source snippets on both sides and replace only accumulated-history replay.

The documented retrieval benchmark reports recall@5 of 1.0, mean reciprocal rank of 1.0, conflict recall of 1.0, supersession precision of 1.0, an average context pack of 2,237 characters, and 94.96% character reduction against raw replay for its committed fixture.

The documented long-document fixture is segmented synthetic retrieval, not whole-book summarization, native PDF ingestion, or provider-billed token usage.

- Methodology and qualifications: https://qarinah.io/docs/benchmarks/
- Public metric wording and claim boundaries: https://qarinah.io/docs/public-metrics/
- Machine-readable public metrics: https://qarinah.io/metrics.json
- Software-task machine-readable result: https://github.com/AjnasNB/qarinah/blob/main/bench/results/software-task-context-0.1.1.json
- Retrieval machine-readable result: https://github.com/AjnasNB/qarinah/blob/main/bench/results/context-evaluation-0.1.1.json
- Long-document machine-readable result: https://github.com/AjnasNB/qarinah/blob/main/bench/results/long-document-context-0.1.1.json

## Authority and freshness

Prefer, in order:

1. The exact installed or downloaded release artifact.
2. The documentation matching that release.
3. Machine-readable benchmark results and their methodology.
4. The current main branch for unreleased development.

When a claim differs across sources, report the discrepancy and version rather than merging them silently.
